import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

df = pd.read_csv("survey.csv")
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
X = pd.get_dummies(df[["age", "income", "region"]])
y = df["smoker"] == "yes"
pred = LogisticRegression().fit(X, y).predict(X)
acc_model = (pred == y).mean()
acc_random = max(y.mean(), 1 - y.mean())
k = int((pred == y).sum())
p = stats.binomtest(k, len(y), acc_random).pvalue
print(f"n = {len(df)}")
print(f"accuracy = {acc_model:.2f}, random baseline accuracy = {acc_random:.2f}, difference = {acc_model - acc_random:.2f}, p = {p:.0e}")
code_output:
n = 1200
accuracy = 0.71, random baseline accuracy = 0.50, difference = 0.21, p = 1e-6
analysis: The classifier outperforms a random baseline (accuracy 0.71 vs 0.50, a difference of 0.21, p = 1e-6).
review: The classifier is better than chance.
